study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract explicitly states the study’s objectives (to investigate how case–control analyses disguise interindividual differences and to map individual-level brain alterations using normative models). The Methods section reiterates the aim to map alterations at the individual level using a normative modeling approach to support precision medicine.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: OBJECTIVES To investigate the degree to which case-control analyses disguise interindividual differences in brain structure among patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder and to map the brain alterations linked to these disorders at the level of individual patients. … we used a normative modeling approach that maps interindividual differences in reference to the healthy range.
cm1_research_objectives.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Abstract (OBJECTIVES); Methods (Introduction to normative modeling)

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This is a NEW normative model. Eligibility criteria for healthy controls are described (randomly sampled from national registries, exclusion of personal/relative psychiatric or alcohol/substance use disorders, and recent cannabis use). Image quality considerations are mentioned (checks for scanner artifacts; image quality metrics analyzed in the supplement), but explicit QC thresholds or exclusion criteria are not fully specified. The final healthy sample size is reported, but reasons for exclusion are not detailed.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Healthy individuals were randomly sampled from national registries if neither they nor their relatives had a psychiatric or alcohol or substance use disorder or any cannabis use during the past 3 months. … We performed additional checks to eliminate the possibility of nuisance effects of scanner artifacts (eg, head motion), medication, and substance abuse confounding our results (eResults in the Supplement). … Regarding image quality, the only significant association we detected was a moderate positive correlation … The image quality metric is quite general and is sensitive to many factors (e.g. head motion or pathology). … This study included … 256 healthy individuals (mean [SD] age, 34 [9.5] years; 140 [54.7%] male).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods–Participants; Results (sample sizes). yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eMethods/eResults (image quality analyses)

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are modeled as covariates in the normative model for healthy individuals. The data were collected on a single 1.5T Siemens scanner at one site, so site effects are not applicable.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: We estimated a normative brain aging model by using gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex … Structural scans were obtained on a 1.5 Tesla Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata scanner …
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods (model inputs). yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eMethods MRI acquisition

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources are clearly described: healthy individuals were sampled from national registries and all participants were recruited under the Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study within a specified time period and location.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study from October 27, 2004, to October 17, 2012. … Healthy individuals were randomly sampled from national registries …

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: PRIMARY data collection with detailed modality, parameters, and equipment: T1-weighted MPRAGE at 1.5T Siemens with TR, TE, TI, FOV, flip angle, matrix, voxel size, and slices reported.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Structural scans were obtained on a 1.5 Tesla Siemens MAGNETOM Sonata scanner … Two T1-weighted images were acquired … MPRAGE … TR = 2730 ms, TE = 3.93 ms, TI = 1000 ms, FOV = 240 mm, flip angle = 7°, matrix = 192 × 256, voxel size = 1.33 × 0.94 × 1 mm, 160 sagittal slices.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described for VBM (CAT12/SPM12; segmentation/normalization/bias correction; 8 mm smoothing) and for FreeSurfer (v5.3 recon-all; surface processing). Quality control procedures are considered indirectly (image quality metrics analyzed; checks for scanner artifacts), but explicit QC thresholds or standardized QC pipeline details are not fully reported.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Raw structural MRI images were preprocessed using the computational analysis version 12 (CAT12) … based on SPM-12. Images were segmented, normalized, and bias-field-corrected … all gray and white matter volumes were smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing kernel. … Structural MRI images were preprocessed using Freesurfer v5.3 … recon-all … We performed additional checks to eliminate the possibility of nuisance effects of scanner artifacts (eg, head motion) … Regarding image quality … image quality metric is quite general …
nm5_data_preprocessing.location: yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eMethods – Estimation of gray/white matter volume; Estimation of cortical thickness/surface area. Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods (artifact checks); yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eResults (image quality)

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They performed internal validation via 10-fold cross-validation on healthy controls to establish the normative range before applying the model to patients.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: … we estimated the normative range for this model in healthy individuals under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model trained on all data to patients.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For this NEW model, there is no indication that an independent external healthy dataset was used for validation. The text describes only internal 10-fold cross-validation in healthy controls and subsequent application to patients.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: … estimated the normative range … under 10-fold cross-validation, then applied the model … to patients. (No external healthy validation dataset described.)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified as Gaussian process regression for normative modeling, with z-scores computed using predictive uncertainty. However, key model settings (e.g., kernel choice, priors) and specific software libraries for the modeling are not detailed.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: Normative models were estimated using gaussian process regression … we used this uncertainty measure to quantify the deviation … by computing a z score for each voxel … All analyses were performed with Python software, version 3.6 …

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Although they emphasize out-of-sample estimation via cross-validation, the paper does not report quantitative performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, calibration/coverage) for the normative model on the reference cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: … it is crucial to estimate performance out of sample. Therefore, we estimated the normative range … under 10-fold cross-validation … (No numerical performance metrics reported.)

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: They used 10-fold cross-validation, but do not report sample sizes or demographic characteristics for each partition (training/validation/test) of the reference cohort.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: … under 10-fold cross-validation … (No reporting of per-partition sizes or demographics.)

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Multiple software and versions are specified (Python 3.6; FreeSurfer v5.3; SPM-12; CAT12). Availability of code, trained models, or data is not stated.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: All analyses were performed with Python software, version 3.6 … Raw structural MRI images were preprocessed using … CAT12 … based on SPM-12 … Structural MRI images were preprocessed using Freesurfer v5.3 …
nm11_reproducibility.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods (software version). yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eMethods (software versions)

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: PRIMARY data collection. Patient eligibility and diagnostic criteria are described (age range, language, IQ>70, SCID for DSM-IV). Image quality considerations are mentioned, but explicit QC standards are not provided. Final sample sizes are reported; reasons for exclusion are not detailed.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Patients (aged 18-65 years) understood and spoke a Scandinavian language, had no history of severe head trauma, and had an IQ above 70. … Psychiatric diagnosis was established using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV Axis I Disorders. … We performed additional checks to eliminate the possibility of nuisance effects of scanner artifacts (eg, head motion) … This study included 218 patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders … and 190 had bipolar disorder …

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses of deviation scores considered clinical covariates beyond demographics, including medication load, substance abuse, disease duration, and cognitive performance.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Finally, we tested for associations between the percentage of extremely deviating voxels and age, disease duration, and cognitive performance. … we regressed the percentage of extreme positive and negative deviations with the normalized total medication load … We then correlated image quality measures and medication load … Further we checked if substance abuse could have influenced our analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods (associations). yoi180064supp1_prod.pdf.md: eResults (medication load and substance abuse analyses)

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection with clear description of recruitment sources (inpatient and outpatient clinics in Oslo), study framework (TOP study), and time period.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: Patients were recruited from inpatient and outpatient clinics in the Oslo area of Norway. All participants were recruited as part of the Thematically Organized Psychosis study from October 27, 2004, to October 17, 2012.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are defined (voxelwise z-scores normalized by predictive uncertainty), thresholds for ‘extreme’ deviations are specified (|z| > 2.6), and clinical implications are discussed, including associations with diagnosis and cognitive/clinical characteristics and the implications for precision medicine.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: … computing a z score for each voxel that reflected the difference between the predicted volume and the true volume normalized by the uncertainty of the prediction. … an extreme value of |z| > 2.6 … The proportion of alterations was associated with diagnosis and cognitive and clinical characteristics within clinical groups. … This study presents a workable route toward precision medicine in psychiatry.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.location: Wolfers2018.pdf.md: Methods (z-score definition); Figure captions (|z| > 2.6); Abstract/Results/Conclusions (clinical associations/implications)
